stem: Write the interval in interval notation.   x < 7

steps: The numbers go from negative infinity up to 7.
Less than, not equal, so 7 gets a parenthesis. Infinity always gets a parenthesis.

stem: Write the interval in interval notation.   x ≥ 2
title: Interval notation: an "or equal to" inequality
steps: The endpoint is included, so it gets a bracket.

stem: Write the interval in interval notation.   −8 < x ≤ 4
title: Interval notation: between two numbers
steps: Strict at negative 8: parenthesis. Or equal at 4: bracket.
Write the left end, then the right end.

stem: Write the interval in interval notation.   the real numbers from 9 through 59
title: Interval notation from words
steps: "Through" includes the endpoints. "Between" leaves them out. "Greater than" and "at most" work like the symbols.

stem: Write the interval shown in interval notation.

steps: arrow left from an open dot at 7 → (−∞, 7)
An arrow means it keeps going. An open dot means 7 isn't included.
A closed dot is included: bracket.
Two pieces are joined with the union symbol.

stem: Write the set of numbers in set-builder notation.   the set of all real numbers except 12

steps: Set-builder notation names the variable, then a bar, then the condition.
Every x except 12: x is not equal to 12.

stem: Write the set of numbers in set-builder notation.   the set of all real numbers greater than 15 and less than 21

steps: Translate the words into an inequality.

stem: Write the set of numbers in set-builder notation.   (−∞, 0] or [8, ∞)

stem: Write the set of numbers in set-builder notation.   [−6, −2)

Write it after the bar. An infinity end just leaves that side open, like x greater than 3.

stem: Sketch the graph of the set of numbers.   {x | x ≠ 2}

Shade everything to the left and to the right.

stem: Sketch the graph of the set of numbers.   {x | x ≤ −2 or x ≥ 3}

stem: Sketch the graph of the set of numbers.   {x | −6 < x ≤ 1}

stem: Let A = [−10, −3) and B = [−8, 2). Write A ∩ B in interval notation. How many integers are in A ∪ B?
